group.title: Feelings
sources: Words and CEFR levels chosen by the authors from general knowledge of English; meanings, examples and sentences are original

Word-list licences checked 2026-10-25: CEFR-J Wordlist 1.5 (Tono Laboratory, TUFS; free with citation, A1-B2) and NGSL/NAWL (CC BY-SA 4.0) were not copied; Oxford 3000 and English Vocabulary Profile terms were not confirmed, so they were not used

words.meaning: Feeling that something bad may happen to you.
examples: My little brother is {afraid} of the dark.
wrong: She was afraid of the kitten, so she hugged it.

words.meaning: Feeling fear.
wrong: He was scared, so he laughed and felt safe.

words.meaning: Feeling that nothing is fun or interesting.
wrong: I was bored because the game was so much fun.

words.meaning: Happy about something.
examples: I’m {glad} you came to my party.
wrong: I was glad you came, so I cried all night.

words.meaning: Feeling bad about something you did.
wrong: I’m sorry, I was so happy I broke your cup.

words.meaning: Not bad; all right.
wrong: I’m okay, I’m very ill and in a lot of pain.

words.meaning: Something you feel inside, like being happy or sad.
wrong: A feeling is a kind of shoe.

words.meaning: Sad; not pleased with how things are.
examples: She is {unhappy} at her new school.
wrong: He was unhappy, so he smiled and sang all day.

words.meaning: Happy about something that happened.
wrong: She was pleased, so she shouted in anger.

words.meaning: Thinking about problems and feeling bad.
wrong: He was worried, so he slept well and felt calm.

words.meaning: Wanting to go to bed.
wrong: I was so sleepy I ran a marathon.

words.meaning: A very happy feeling.
examples: She jumped for {joy} when she won.
wrong: He cried with joy at the very sad news.

words.meaning: The bad feeling you have when you think you are in danger.
examples: He has a {fear} of big dogs.
wrong: She felt fear, so she smiled and relaxed.

words.meaning: A drop of water that comes from your eye when you cry.
wrong: Tears came out of her ears.

words.meaning: To make lines on your face when you are angry or unhappy.
wrong: She frowned because she was so happy.

words.meaning: To open your mouth wide because you are tired.
examples: He {yawned} at the end of the long day.
wrong: I yawned because I was full of energy.

words.meaning: To make a very loud, high sound.
examples: She {screamed} when she saw the spider.
wrong: He screamed in a very quiet, soft voice.

words.meaning: Angry.
examples: Mom is {mad} at me for being late.
wrong: She was mad at me, so she gave me a hug and a kiss.

words.meaning: To be less sick or less sad than before.
wrong: I feel better, so I need to stay in bed longer.

words.meaning: Calm and not worried.
wrong: I felt relaxed, so my hands shook with worry.

words.meaning: The feeling of being glad and full of joy.
wrong: Her happiness made her cry with sadness.

words.meaning: The feeling you have when you are unhappy.
wrong: Her sadness made her laugh and dance.

words.meaning: Something you did not know would happen.
wrong: It was a surprise, so we knew about it all week.

words.meaning: A time when you feel angry or not happy.
wrong: He was in a bad mood, so he smiled at everyone.

words.meaning: A time when you feel happy and friendly.
wrong: She was in a good mood, so she shouted at everyone.

words.meaning: Making you feel afraid.
wrong: The scary movie made me feel safe and happy.

words.meaning: Quite good; a short answer to say you are fine.
wrong: "Not bad," he said, crying in pain.

words.meaning: A question you ask to learn if someone is well.
wrong: "How are you?" she asked, to learn the time.

words.meaning: Afraid of something.
examples: The cat is {frightened} of the dog.
wrong: She was frightened, so she felt brave and calm.

words.meaning: Having strong, warm feelings for someone.
examples: They are {in love} and want to get married.
wrong: They were in love, so they never wanted to see each other.

words.meaning: A very strong, warm feeling for someone.
examples: A mother’s {love} for her baby is strong.
wrong: His love for her made him want to hurt her.

words.meaning: Words you say to tell someone to stay calm.
wrong: "Don’t worry," she said, to make him more afraid.

words.meaning: To enjoy yourself.
wrong: We had fun, so we were bored all day.

words.meaning: A wide, happy look on your face.
examples: She had a {big smile} on her face.
wrong: He had a big smile because he was very sad.

words.meaning: A dream that makes you feel afraid.
examples: I had a {bad dream} about a monster.
wrong: I had a bad dream, so I woke up happy and calm.

words.meaning: A very scary dream.
examples: The child woke up after a {nightmare}.
wrong: I had a nightmare, a lovely dream about candy.

words.meaning: To laugh in a quiet, silly way.
wrong: She giggled because the news made her so sad.

words.meaning: To be happy or well.
examples: I {feel good} after a long walk.
wrong: I feel good, so I’m going to the doctor.

words.meaning: The strong feeling of being angry.
wrong: He shouted in anger because he was so happy.

words.meaning: The sad feeling when someone is unkind to you.
examples: Her mean words gave me {hurt feelings}.
wrong: His kind words gave me hurt feelings.
